products.title: Viva Italia
products.body_html:
VIVA ITALIA Four Italian Wines · From Veneto to Tuscany


01 Cantina del Garda Soave Classico

DOC Soave Classico · Veneto, Italy · 100% Garganega · 91pts Falstaff

◆ Grown on volcanic hillside soils in the Classico zone — the heartland of Soave — and aged six months in steel to preserve every bit of freshness the terroir gives. Pale yellow with green-gold reflections in the glass.

◆ The nose is delicate and characterful: chamomile, elderflower and a hint of cherry blossom. On the palate it’s harmonious and fruity with white peach front and centre, then a distinct mineral backbone and a flint-edged finish that lingers.

◆ 91 points from Falstaff and four stars to its name — this is Italian white wine done properly. Works from aperitivo through to fish, white meat, or a bowl of good ramen.

 

02 Alessandro Rivetto Langhe Nascetta Albori

DOC Langhe · Piedmont, Italy · 100% Nascetta · Hand Harvested

◆ Nascetta is one of Piedmont’s rarest indigenous white grapes — nearly extinct until a handful of producers in the Langhe brought it back. Rivetto is one of the best. Brilliant straw-yellow, hand-harvested, fermented slow and cold at 15–18°C.

◆ Semi-aromatic in the best possible way: delicate flowers, salvia and thyme on the nose with a savouriness that builds as it opens up in the glass. Great minerality running through the whole palate.

◆ This is the wine in the pack that people won’t recognise — and that’s exactly the point. Pour it, watch them puzzle over it, then tell them what it is. Perfect with antipasti, raw fish, or on its own.


03 Menicucci Chianti DOCG

DOCG Chianti · Tuscany, Italy · Sangiovese, Cabernet Sauvignon & Merlot

◆ From the rich soils of Cerreto and Montalbano in Tuscany — Sangiovese doing the heavy lifting at 90%, with Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot rounding out the edges. Hand-selected, gently pressed, fermented at controlled temperatures for 10 days.

◆ Intense ruby red with violet reflections. The nose is warm and generous — berry jam with a savoury undercurrent. On the palate it’s wide, balanced and full of personality with a structure that tells you this is proper Chianti, not a supermarket blend.

◆ The kind of bottle you open with a board of cured meats and end up finishing before the main course arrives. Equally good alongside roasted meats, hearty pasta or aged cheese.


04 Benedetti Valpolicella Superiore Ripasso Classico

DOC Valpolicella · Veneto, Italy · Corvina, Corvinone, Rondinella & Molinara · 14.5%

◆ Ripasso is one of Italy’s great winemaking tricks: take a good Valpolicella and referment it on the leftover skins of Amarone. You get deeper colour, richer aromatics and more alcohol without the price tag of the Amarone itself.

Benedetti do this from one of the five historic communities of Valpolicella Classica.

◆ Ruby red with garnet reflections. Full and complex on the nose — cherry, wild berries, spice and a whisper of cream. On the palate it’s persistent, soft and enveloping with elegant tannins and a long cherry finish.

◆ 16–18 months in French oak, 14.5% ABV, and the kind of weight and complexity that makes it the natural closer of this pack. Big glasses, 18°C, and something substantial on the plate.

products.title: Weeknight Pours
products.body_html:
WEEKNIGHT POURS

Two Whites, Two Reds · France & Italy


01 Cellier des Demoiselles Chardonnay

IGP Pays d’Oc · Languedoc, France · 100% Chardonnay · Machine Harvested at Night

◆ Chardonnay grown on clay-limestone with a limestone glaze in the south of France — picked at night to preserve freshness, then fermented clean in steel. Pale in colour with green highlights and an expressive nose of grapefruit, acidulous notes and a touch of white fruit.

◆ Very fresh in the mouth, pleasantly light and well balanced — this is a Chardonnay that’s easy to love without needing a wine education to enjoy it. No heavy oak, no fuss.

◆ The kind of bottle you reach for on a Tuesday with pasta, grilled prawns or a simple veal dish. Serve at 12°C and drink young while it’s at its most vivid.


02 Tenimenti Civa Pinot Grigio Ronc Laris

DOC Friuli · Friuli Colli Orientali, Italy · 100% Pinot Grigio · “Ponca” Soils

◆ Grown on the ancient marl and sandstone “Ponca” soils of Friuli Colli Orientali — one of Italy’s best addresses for white wine. Harvested in the cool of early September morning, soft pressed, fermented at 16–18°C for 15 days.

◆ Pale lemon with amber reflections. The nose opens with intensity: citrus, apricot and linden flowers. On the palate it’s medium-bodied with great balance — ripe cherry, golden apple and mango with a nice sapidity and a soft finish that lingers.

◆ A Pinot Grigio that goes well beyond the category’s reputation for blandness. Versatile enough for white meat, fish, cured meats or egg dishes — and interesting enough to drink on its own.

03 Terra Vallona IGP Comte Tolosan Rouge

IGP Comte Tolosan · South West France · Merlot & Cabernets · 14%

◆ From Cave du Marmandais in the heart of the French South West — a co-operative with deep roots in the region and a straightforward philosophy: make wines that are genuinely enjoyable without overthinking them.

◆ Merlot leads, Cabernet supports. The result is a crisp, fruit-forward red with strawberry and blackcurrant on the nose, a touch of spice, and a palate that’s round, generous and built on fresh fruit rather than heavy tannin.

◆ This is the bottle you open when dinner is already on the table and nobody wants to wait. Great with red meat, cheese, or anything off the barbecue. Best at 16–18°C.


04 Menicucci Montepulciano d’Abruzzo

DOC Montepulciano d’Abruzzo · Abruzzo, Italy · 100% Montepulciano · 13.5%

◆ Montepulciano d’Abruzzo is one of Italy’s most reliable red grapes — deep colour, generous fruit, soft tannins, and a price that never makes you wince. Menicucci harvest mid-September, macerate for 7–8 days for colour and structure, then age three months on fine lees.

◆ Deep, intense ruby with violet highlights. The bouquet is pleasant and fruity, and on the palate it’s dry and round with a full-bodied finish, soft tannins and just enough acidity to keep it fresh and food-friendly.

◆ The closer of this pack — weight, warmth and character without demanding anything of you in return. Pasta or red meat is all it needs. Serve at 18–20°C in a decent-sized glass.

products.title: Pretty in Pink
products.body_html:
PRETTY IN PINK

Four Rosé Wines · From Corsica to Beaujolais

01 Terra Vecchia GR20 Rosé

IGP Île de Beauté · Corsica, France · Niellucciu & Sciaccarellu

◆ Named for Europe’s most demanding hiking trail — and it earns it. Pale salmon-copper in the glass with a nose of red rhubarb, white peach and green pear edged with white pepper. This is what a Corsican morning smells like.

◆ On the palate the freshness hits immediately: clean, precise acidity built on a mineral backbone, with citrus and spiced white pepper weaving through the mid-palate.

◆ A lick of ginger on the finish keeps it vivacious and alive. Sauvage by name, sauvage by nature — and honestly one of the most characterful rosés in this pack.


02 Umathum Rosa Rosé Saignée

Burgenland, Austria · Zweigelt, Sankt Laurent & Blaufränkisch · Biodynamic

◆ Made by the traditional saignée method — red grapes macerated on their skins before fermentation to pull colour, aroma and soft tannin from the berries. The result is a rosé with genuine depth and a red-wine backbone.

◆ Brilliant raspberry red in the glass, with raspberries, cherries and red currants on the nose. Fruity and juicy on the palate with impressions of gooseberry and medium acidity that keeps it fresh.

◆ This is not a delicate summer sipping rosé — it has structure, character and the kind of finish that makes you reach for another glass. Farmed biodynamically from vines up to 45 years old.


03 Diwald Zweigelt Rosé

Wagram, Austria · Zweigelt & Pinot Noir · Organic since 1976

◆ Diwald set out to make a serious rosé, not sugar water — and they’ve delivered. Part saignée, part whole-bunch pressed from cooler sites, with spontaneous fermentation in tank. Zweigelt gives the fruit, Pinot Noir gives the tension.

◆ Abundant cherry on the nose and palate with crisp acidity and a body that actually shows up — this is a rosé with enough going on to hold its own at the dinner table, not just the aperitivo hour.

◆ One of Austria’s oldest organic wine estates, farming without chemicals since 1976. The fact that it drinks this well is not an accident.


04 Croifolie Rosé Labise

AOP Beaujolais-Villages · Beaujolais, France · 100% Gamay · Guide Hachette ★ 2024

◆ Four generations of the same family farming 6 hectares in Salles-Arbuissonnas — Gamay from clay-granitic soils, harvested by hand and aged on fine lees for 2–3 months before bottling.

◆ Shiny with golden-pink highlights in the glass, fruity and aromatic on the nose, and tender on the palate with a lovely acidity-to-fruit balance that makes it dangerously easy to drink.

◆ Five consecutive Guide Hachette stars across five vintages. That’s not luck — that’s consistency. A go-everywhere, please-everyone rosé from one of Beaujolais’ most reliable small estates.

Serve chilled · 8–12°C · Best enjoyed in good company

We are pioneers of the Austrian organic wine farming movement. Our roots lie in the Wagram wine region, where the younger generation has since taken over the reins. We like Grüner Veltliner and Riesling. But we also like rare grape varieties, such as Frühroter Veltliner, and we love cool, refreshing red wines. All that we need is a lot of know-how, gut-feel, patience and love for wine.

Hans and Paula Diwald grew up in the 1960s, both on a farm. In 1972, they took over the business and restructured it. Since 1976, they have become true pioneers by endeavouring something unthinkable: converting to organic farming practices. Back then there was no official certification yet, only a handful of kindred spirits. Paula and Hans used to be on the receiving end of condescending smiles, but today they are considered among the pioneers of a whole movement. We currently farm 20 ha of vines on our farm and export our wine to 18 countries, on 3 continents.

In 2006, Martin Diwald joined the estate. After studying at the Institute of Viticulture and Pomology in Klosterneuburg and completing numerous internships, he was pushed straight into the deep end. He took great joy in experimenting and has never lost that enthusiasm. For example, his experiments with spontaneous fermentation were so successful that already in his second year all the wines were fermented in this way.

products.title: Taruguin 2019
products.body_html:
2019 Vintage.

Year 2019 was defined by heat and drought. After year 2018 with lots of rains, Nature seems to offset with hot days and our vines hardly resisted and followed its natural lifecycle. This vintage gave us lovely lush and deep wines.

 

The vines bud break was around last days of April, as other times in our region. That is a magical preciseness from our plants that we find admirable. During the spring, the usual frosts in the area did not miss their appointment during the first fortnight of May, and even in June.

Summer was extremely hot with very few rainy days, that finally appeared on September. Fortunately that rain helps the plants to complete maturation and earn weight and must yield. The extraordinary adaptability of the hardworking Soria vineyards shone in this vintage with fabulous results.

 

Winemaking.

The harvest was carried out between October 1st and 5th, we vatted the grapes in stainless steel tanks of 1,500 and 2,500 litres, without the addition of any sulphur, where fermentations took place with average macerations of 12 days. Fermentations occurred spontaneously without adding selected yeasts. We apply punching down and pumping over at the beginning of the process, intervening minimally on the cap for the rest of the fermentation.

Aging.

 

We rack the wine, removing the largest lees, and selecting the finest to accompany the wine during its aging in used 225-litre French oak barrels. The wine completed a total aging of 13 months, with racking twice a year.

 

The bottling was in June 2021, the total production was 6,160 bottles (0.75l).

products.title: Taruguin 2019
products.body_html:
2019 Vintage.

Year 2019 was defined by heat and drought. After year 2018 with lots of rains, Nature seems to offset with hot days and our vines hardly resisted and followed its natural lifecycle. This vintage gave us lovely lush and deep wines.

 

The vines bud break was around last days of April, as other times in our region. That is a magical preciseness from our plants that we find admirable. During the spring, the usual frosts in the area did not miss their appointment during the first fortnight of May, and even in June.

Summer was extremely hot with very few rainy days, that finally appeared on September. Fortunately that rain helps the plants to complete maturation and earn weight and must yield. The extraordinary adaptability of the hardworking Soria vineyards shone in this vintage with fabulous results.

 

Winemaking.

The harvest was carried out between October 1st and 5th, we vatted the grapes in stainless steel tanks of 1,500 and 2,500 litres, without the addition of any sulphur, where fermentations took place with average macerations of 12 days. Fermentations occurred spontaneously without adding selected yeasts. We apply punching down and pumping over at the beginning of the process, intervening minimally on the cap for the rest of the fermentation.

Aging.

 

We rack the wine, removing the largest lees, and selecting the finest to accompany the wine during its aging in used 225-litre French oak barrels. The wine completed a total aging of 13 months, with racking twice a year.

 

The bottling was in June 2021, the total production was 6,160 bottles (0.75l).

products.title: Organic Tunisian Lemon Mint - 100g
products.body_html:
Superb lemon freshness intermingles with flavory Rooibos. Light mint finish.

Tunisians love their lemons. In all probability, they've been an important part of their diet since the place was known as Carthage, at least as far back as 814 BC. For a time, Carthage, in what is now the Tunisian capital of Tunis, was part of the Roman Empire and supplied lemons to Roman citizens from Rome to Londinium. Mint, although its history in Tunisia isn't quite as long as the lemon's, definitely holds a vaulted place in Tunisian culture. Visit any shop, home or office there and the first thing you'll be offered is a hot cup of mint tea.

What doesn't have much of a history in Tunisia is Rooibos, an evergreen shrub native to South Africa, thousands of kilometers away to the south. We've decided to change all that by introducing this fabulous blend of Tunisian lemon, mint and Rooibos. We're 100% certain they'll be talking about this one a few thousand years from now! An incredibly flavorful cup with herbal notes tempered by sweet lemon and mint.

What makes rooibos tea particularly good for your belly is a unique and powerful flavonoid called Aspalathin. According to South African researchers, polyphenols and flavonoids found in the plant inhibit adipogenesis–the formation of new fat cells–by as much as 22 percent. The chemicals also help aid fat metabolism. As an added bonus, Rooibos is naturally sweet, so you won't need to add sugar.

products.title: Detox, Cleanse & Refresh - 100g
products.body_html:
Detox,cleanse, and refresh your body and soul. Pleasant tending fruity cup with a delicious ginger finish.

Modern life, in many ways, is toxic. We take for granted that much of our day-to-day isn't always great for the body, spirit and mind. From air pollution to alcohol, processed food to smartphones, our bodies are bombarded by negative inputs every time we leave the house. No wonder the news is filled with stories about people stepping back to go on a cleanse - our brains and bodies need a break!

To do our part, we've crafted Detox, Cleanse & Refresh, an herbal tea with detoxification in mind. Borrowing from the ancient practices of Ayurveda, Native American remedies and sacred herbology, we've sourced a list of ingredients that reads like a what's what of detoxifying herbs. Let's examine a few of them.

Tulsi, commonly known as holy basil, is not only a source of Vitamin K, important for transporting calcium through the body, it is also said to aid the digestive system and promote weight loss. Licorice is also said to relieve digestive issues, along with ginger and Burdock root, considered by some natural health practitioners, to function as twin powerhouses when it comes to easing nausea. Additionally, Cleanse & Refresh also incorporates a selection of antioxidant rich flower petals, including Dandelion, said to aid in cleansing the liver.

Need to slow down and detoxify? You've found your tea. (Naturally caffeine-free.)
